Let \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). By the definition of the realization fiber,
\[
 \bigl(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K}\bigr)
 =\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B),
 \qquad
 \widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The admissibility of \(B\) is exactly the hypothesis of the graphical replacement lemma. Applying that lemma to (1) gives
\[
 A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)
\tag{2}
\]
and, for every \(j=0,\ldots,K\),
\[
 \operatorname{skel}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))
 =\operatorname{skel}(M_j(\eta)),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{UC}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))
 =\operatorname{UC}(M_j(\eta))
\tag{3}
\]
on the complete domain \(U_j\). In particular, (3) includes all adjacencies and unshielded colliders involving \(\zeta_j\) when \(j\ge1\).

Membership in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) in (1) supplies positive selection probability, so the observational selected law is defined; it also supplies non-target kernel stability and faithfulness of every pooled selected law. By the definition of the oracle signature, (3) therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)
 =\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_j(\widetilde\eta)),
         \operatorname{UC}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))\bigr)_{j=0}^{K}
 =\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2) and (4), together with the definitions of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), imply
\[
 \widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta).
\tag{5}
\]
Finally, the target-and-descendant conclusion of the graphical replacement lemma gives, for every \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
 \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\tag{6}
\]
This proves the asserted property of every member of \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). If that set is nonempty, choosing any member proves the final existence implication. At no point was \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)=\kappa(\eta)\) used. \(\square\)

Write \(A=A(\eta)\) and let \(e\) be the endpoint specified in the statement. The set \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\) is nonempty: indeed, \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and \(A(\eta)=A(\eta)\), so the definition of the fixed-\(A\) fiber gives \(\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), and hence \(\mu_\eta(e)\in\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\).

We next prove the inclusion. Take an arbitrary \(\eta'\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\). Because \(u\in A(\eta')=A\), the indicator-neighbor formula in the twin-MAG interface gives, for every \(\ell\in[K]\),
\[
 u\in Z_\ell
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\in F_\ell(\eta').
\tag{1}
\]
The same interface's endpoint cases for the intervention-created edge \(uv\) imply
\[
 \mu_{\eta'}(e)=\mathtt{arrow}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in Z_k,
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \mu_{\eta'}(e)=\mathtt{tail}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 u\notin Z_k\ \text{ or }\
 u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta')}(v).
\tag{3}
\]
To sharpen the second alternative, suppose \(u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta')}(v)\) and take a nonempty directed basal path
\[
 u=x_0\to x_1\to\cdots\to x_r=v.
\tag{4}
\]
The set \(A(\eta')\) is ancestor closed among observed vertices: by its definition, \(v\in A(\eta')\) is an ancestor of an observed parent of a childless selection node, and every \(x_i\), being an ancestor of \(v\), has the same property. Thus \(x_i\in A\) for all \(i\). Every edge in (4) is an observational adjacency by the basal-edge clause of the twin-MAG interface, and hence belongs to \(H[A]\). If \(\ell\in\sigma(x_i)\), then \(x_i\in Z_\ell\); by (1), \(x_i\in F_\ell(\eta')\). Descendant closure of
\[
 F_\ell(\eta')=\operatorname{de}_{G_0(\eta')}(T_\ell(\eta'))\cap V
\]
and the edge \(x_i\to x_{i+1}\) give \(x_{i+1}\in F_\ell(\eta')\), and (1) applied to \(x_{i+1}\in A\) gives \(x_{i+1}\in Z_\ell\). Therefore
\[
 \sigma(x_i)\subseteq\sigma(x_{i+1})
 \quad\text{for }i=0,\ldots,r-1.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) exhibit a nonempty directed path from \(u\) to \(v\) in \(L_A\), so
\[
 u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta')}(v)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (2), (3), and (6) proves \(\mu_{\eta'}(e)\in\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)\). Since \(\eta'\) was arbitrary,
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\tag{7}
\]
If \(u\notin Z_k\), the right side of (7) is the singleton \(\{\mathtt{tail}\}\); if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=0\), it is \(\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\). Nonemptiness in (7) proves equality in both singleton cases.

It remains to establish the graphical assertions in the two-mark case. Suppose \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=1\). Let \(B_0\) have vertex set \(A\) and no edges. It is acyclic, is a subgraph of \(H[A]\), respects every signature inclusion vacuously, and creates no unshielded collider. In the replacement basal graph there is no directed path from \(u\) to the distinct vertex \(v\): there is no directed edge within \(A\), and a path that left \(A\) and later returned to \(v\in A\) would make an exterior observed vertex an ancestor of \(v\), hence an ancestor of a selection parent, contradicting the definition of \(A\). The graphical replacement lemma gives that \(u\in Z_k\) is affected in the replacement. The endpoint cases in the twin-MAG interface then give an arrowhead at \(u\), whether \(v\) is unaffected, is an ancestor of \(u\), or is affected and ancestrally incomparable with \(u\).

By finite reachability, choose a simple directed path
\[
 P:u=y_0\to y_1\to\cdots\to y_s=v
\]
in \(L_A\), and let \(B_P\) contain exactly these directed edges. A directed simple path is acyclic. Its edges lie in \(H[A]\) and satisfy \(\sigma(y_i)\subseteq\sigma(y_{i+1})\) by the definition of \(L_A\). No vertex has two incoming \(B_P\)-edges, so \(B_P\) creates no unshielded collider. Thus \(B_P\) is admissible. In its replacement basal graph, \(u\) is an ancestor of \(v\). Since \(u\in Z_k\), it is affected; descendant closure then also makes \(v\) affected. The twin-MAG endpoint rule therefore gives the orientation \(u\to v\), in particular a tail at \(e\).

Applying the graphical replacement lemma to \(B_0\) and \(B_P\) proves, without choosing kernels, that both graphical specifications preserve \(A\) and every skeleton and unshielded collider on every full \(U_j\), including all indicator-involving instances. If both realization fibers are nonempty, choose
\[
 \eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0),
 \qquad
 \eta_{\mathtt{tail}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P).
\]
The conditional replacement-preservation lemma places both choices in \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), and the preceding graphical endpoint calculation gives their indicated opposite marks. Both marks therefore belong to \(\mathcal M_A\); together with (7), this proves \(\mathcal M_A=\mathcal G_A=\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\). The retained-edge sanity proposition shows separately that no target-membership equivalence can be extended to adjacencies in \(H\). \(\square\)

Fix a reported endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\). There are two exhaustive cases because the closure assigns either a definite mark or a circle.

Suppose first that \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\). Soundness, the first part of the observable unknown-\(A\) extension condition, gives
\[
 \mu_\xi(e)=m
 \qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O).
\tag{1}
\]
By the definition of the canonical SI-PAG, (1) implies
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m.
\tag{2}
\]

Suppose instead that \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\). Apply the extension property once with \(m=\mathtt{tail}\) and once with \(m=\mathtt{arrow}\). This supplies compatible bases \(\xi_{e,\mathtt{tail}},\xi_{e,\mathtt{arrow}}\) and admissible graphs \(B_{e,\mathtt{tail}},B_{e,\mathtt{arrow}}\). Faithful realization makes both corresponding realization fibers nonempty. Choose
\[
 \widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}}
 \in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,\mathtt{tail}},B_{e,\mathtt{tail}}),
 \qquad
 \widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}
 \in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,\mathtt{arrow}},B_{e,\mathtt{arrow}}).
\tag{3}
\]
The conditional replacement-preservation lemma gives
\[
 \widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}},
 \widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}
 \in\mathcal C(\mathcal O),
\tag{4}
\]
and the mark clause of the extension property gives
\[
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}}}(e)=\mathtt{tail},
 \qquad
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}}(e)=\mathtt{arrow}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus the mark is not invariant over \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and the canonical definition yields
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (2) and (6) cover every endpoint, proving
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O).
\]

Under the additional uniform polynomial-time premise-decider condition, the conditional polynomial-saturation proposition applies directly to the fixed finite list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\). It gives at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict endpoint updates and polynomial total running time. This computational conclusion is conditional on the same premises and makes no global compatibility-fiber enumeration. \(\square\)

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and an admissible replacement graph \(B\). Suppose a nonempty open set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^r\) parameterizes finite-alphabet ambient tuples \(\eta_\theta\) with graph and target components \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\). Assume that every regime law factorizes through finite local kernels over the replacement basal DAG, that the same local kernel is used in every regime at each non-target vertex, that the common childless observed-parent selection nodes are generated before intervention, and that \(\Pr_{\eta_\theta}(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\). For \(k\in[K]\), write \(p_{\theta,k}\) for the mass function of \(P_{\eta_\theta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), and let the replacement MAG be the latent projection on \(U_k\) determined by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\). Assume also that every \(p_{\theta,k}\)-cell is strictly positive and rational in \(\theta\), with denominator positive on \(\Theta\), and that \(m\)-separation in each replacement MAG implies the corresponding conditional independence for every \(\theta\in\Theta\). The graphical replacement lemma supplies acyclicity, causal sufficiency among measured vertices, and the required selection-node structure. For every \(k\in[K]\), every disjoint \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\), and every cell assignment \(a\), clear positive denominators in
\[
 p_{\theta,k}(r_1,r_2,w)p_{\theta,k}(w)
 -p_{\theta,k}(r_1,w)p_{\theta,k}(r_2,w)
\]
and denote the resulting polynomial by \(q_{k,R_1,R_2,W,a}\). There is a parameter \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) for which all pooled laws are simultaneously faithful if and only if, for every query that is \(m\)-connected in its replacement MAG, at least one of its polynomials \(q_{k,R_1,R_2,W,a}\) is not the zero polynomial. At such a parameter, the tuple is a member of \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). Hence simultaneous faithful realization is reduced to the atomic nontriviality of one determinant polynomial per \(m\)-connected query.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because every alphabet and every \(U_k\) is finite, there are finitely many indices \((k,R_1,R_2,W,a)\). Strict positivity gives \(p_{\theta,k}(w)>0\). Therefore the elementary finite-table criterion for conditional independence gives
\[
 R_1\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}R_2\mid W
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 p_{\theta,k}(r_1,r_2,w)p_{\theta,k}(w)
 =p_{\theta,k}(r_1,w)p_{\theta,k}(r_2,w)
\]
for every cell assignment. Since all denominators are positive on \(\Theta\), clearing them preserves each equality and yields exactly the stated polynomial equations.

Assume first that every \(m\)-connected query has at least one nonzero determinant polynomial. Choose one such polynomial \(q_Q\) for each \(m\)-connected query \(Q\), and set
\[
 Q_\ast(\theta):=\prod_Q q_Q(\theta).
\]
The product is finite. The polynomial ring \(\mathbb R[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r]\) is an integral domain, so \(Q_\ast\) is not the zero polynomial. We now prove directly that it cannot vanish on all of the nonempty open set \(\Theta\). For \(r=1\), a nonzero univariate polynomial has only finitely many roots and hence cannot vanish on an open interval. Inductively, write a polynomial in \(r\) variables as a polynomial in \(\theta_r\) whose coefficients are polynomials in the first \(r-1\) variables. If it vanishes on an open box, then for every point in the box's projection the resulting univariate polynomial vanishes on an interval, so all coefficient polynomials vanish on that open projection. The induction hypothesis makes every coefficient the zero polynomial, a contradiction. Every nonempty open set contains an open box, proving the claim.

Choose \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) with \(Q_\ast(\theta^\star)\ne0\). For every \(m\)-connected query, its selected determinant is nonzero, so that query is not conditionally independent. By the assumed Markov direction, every \(m\)-separated query is conditionally independent. These two implications establish faithfulness simultaneously for all \(k\in[K]\). All other required class properties were imposed on the parameterized tuples, so \(\eta_{\theta^\star}\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\); its graph and target components equal \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), whence \(\eta_{\theta^\star}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\).

Conversely, suppose \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) gives simultaneous faithfulness. For an \(m\)-connected query, faithfulness rules out conditional independence. By the finite-table criterion, some cell determinant is nonzero at \(\theta^\star\); after multiplication by its positive denominator, the corresponding polynomial is nonzero at \(\theta^\star\) and therefore is not the zero polynomial. This proves necessity and completes the equivalence. Strictly positive normalized local tables with identical tables copied across regimes at every non-target vertex show separately that factorization, non-target stability, and positive selection probability are compatible constraints. They do not prove the atomic determinant nontriviality on the shared-response-function twin space, which is precisely the residual question. \(\square\)
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma proves the finite algebraic exceptional-set reduction while isolating, rather than assuming, the unresolved atomic nontriviality step.
added_lemmas.gap: It does not assert that the equality-constrained shared-response-function parameter space has a nonzero determinant for every m-connected query.
added_lemmas.consumer: The faithful-realization open question uses it to state the remaining obstruction at atomic determinant granularity.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and an admissible \(B\) in the sense of the graphical replacement lemma. Does the replacement graphical specification admit finite-alphabet shared-response-function kernels with positive selection probability and non-target kernel stability such that every pooled selected law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), \(k\in[K]\), is faithful to its replacement MAG? For any supplied finite-dimensional rational parameterization satisfying the Markov direction, this existence question reduces to atomic determinant nontriviality: for every \(k\in[K]\) and every conditional-independence query that is \(m\)-connected in the replacement MAG, at least one cleared conditional-independence determinant must be a nonzero polynomial on the equality-constrained shared-response-function parameter space. The finite-union exceptional-set argument is valid once these atomic certificates are available; the atomic certificates themselves remain open.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional existence claim requires atomic determinant nontriviality on an equality-constrained shared-response-function twin space. The frozen assumptions and unrestricted-DAG generic faithfulness do not supply that certificate, so the honest post-image is an open realization question plus the proved exceptional-set reduction.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), every admissible \(B\), and every \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\), one has \(A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\), \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\), and hence \(\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\). Every adjacency and unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, is preserved, and for every \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
 \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\]
Consequently, if \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\ne\varnothing\), then a fully specified faithful replacement witness with all these properties exists. No equality between \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(\kappa(\eta)\) is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Graphical preservation proves every asserted property for any member of the realization fiber, but does not prove that the fiber is nonempty. Replacing unconditional existence by a universal member characterization and an explicit nonemptiness implication removes exactly the unresolved realization step.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\), where \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) is present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Let \(e\) be the endpoint at \(u\) on \(uv\). Then
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq \mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\]
Thus, if \(u\notin Z_k\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}\); if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\). If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the empty graph \(B_0\) on \(A(\eta)\) and the directed-edge graph \(B_P\) of any simple \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) are admissible and give two common-basal graphical replacement specifications preserving \(A(\eta)\) and every regime skeleton and unshielded collider on the full domains \(U_j\). The former has an arrowhead and the latter a tail at \(e\). In this two-mark case,
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\]
Here \(u\in Z_k\) denotes direct targeting or indirect affectedness within \(A(\eta)\), not necessarily \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this intervention-created-edge bracket.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The faithful-model mark set is always nonempty and is contained in the stated graphical bracket, which gives exact singleton cases. In the two-mark case the two graphical specifications are proved, but equality with the two-element bracket requires nonemptiness of both realization fibers.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Does there exist a single finite rule list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with schemata independent of \(D\) and \(K\), that uses only the observable premises permitted by \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), is sound over every compatibility fiber, and has the following unknown-\(A\) graphical extension property? For every residual reported circle endpoint and each requested mark \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), the extension supplies a compatible base model and an admissible replacement graph, without guessing \(A\) in a rule premise or invoking a global feasibility query, such that every fully specified member of the corresponding realization fiber has mark \(m\). The affirmative answer must preserve the complete observational and pooled-law signatures, including indicator-involving adjacencies and unshielded colliders, and must respect
\[
 Z_k=T_k\cup\bigl((F_k\setminus T_k)\cap A\bigr)
\]
without setting \(T_k=Z_k\). Together with an affirmative answer to the faithful-realization question, this observable graphical extension property implies the conditional completeness theorem; neither affirmative answer is established here.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: No fixed local rule list or unknown-selection common-exterior extension theorem is available. The revised question isolates that observable graphical extension and records that faithful promotion is a separate open premise.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) be a candidate finite rule list whose schemata are independent of \(D\) and \(K\). Fix a compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\). Assume the following two conditions.

First, faithful realization holds: for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and every graph \(B\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma, \(\operatorname{Real}(\xi,B)\ne\varnothing\).

Second, the observable unknown-\(A\) extension property holds: the closure is sound, meaning that a definite mark \(m\) at \(e\) in \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) satisfies \(\mu_\xi(e)=m\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\); and, for every endpoint \(e\) left circular and every \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), there are \(\xi_{e,m}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and a graph \(B_{e,m}\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma such that every \(\widetilde\xi\in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m})\) has \(\mu_{\widetilde\xi}(e)=m\). The rule premises themselves use no latent \(A(\xi)\), compatible-model query, or global enumerator.

Then
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)
\]
on all reported observed endpoints. If, in addition, every rule premise and path predicate is uniformly decidable in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), then saturation is polynomial and makes at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. This is a conditional implication; it does not assert that either open condition or such a rule list exists.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Existence of a sound complete fixed rule list and opposing faithful witnesses is not proved. The endpointwise implication from faithful realization plus an observable unknown-A extension property to canonical equality is fully provable and is the strongest honest same-class result requested by the orchestrator.

proposed.name: Fixed-A faithful and graphical mark sets
proposed.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created adjacency \(uv\) with \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), let \(e=(k,u\mid uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\) denote the endpoint at \(u\). Define the fully specified-model mark set
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 :=\{\mu_{\widetilde\eta}(e):
       \widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\}
\]
and the graphical mark bracket
\[
 \mathcal G_A(u,v;k):=
 \begin{cases}
 \{\mathtt{tail}\},
   &u\notin Z_k,\\
 \{\mathtt{arrow}\},
   &u\in Z_k\ \text{and}\
     \operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0,\\
 \{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\},
   &u\in Z_k\ \text{and}\
     \operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The set \(\mathcal M_A\) ranges only over fully specified faithful members of the fixed-\(A\) compatibility fiber; \(\mathcal G_A\) is computed from the graphical quantities for the fixed fiber.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition separates the observed-law faithful-model mark set from the graphical outer bracket and makes the conditional equality precise.

proposed.name: Observable synchronized Zhang--Dai construction handle
proposed.construction: \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the following observable rule-development program. Start from Zhang's rules R0--R10 on the observational signature on \(U_0=V\), associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_\eta(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), and on each \(k\in[K]\) full signature on \(U_k\), associated with the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\). Compute \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) from intervention-created adjacencies and observational-unshielded-noncollider closure, and investigate propagation of forbidden signature transitions along shortest uncovered paths certified by \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\). Enforce Dai et al.'s disjunction \(Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta))\) only as a witness obligation, without identifying \(T_k(\eta)\) with \(Z_k\). The latent objects \(L_{A(\eta)}\), \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), and \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) may be used only in a semantic extension proof after a compatible base model is chosen; none is a rule premise. The handle specifies constraints on a prospective finite list in \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\); it does not assert that such a sound and complete list has been derived.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle is a development program and must not claim that it already derives the missing finite complete list.

proposed.statement:
For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), every admissible \(B\), and every \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\), one has \(A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\), \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\), and hence \(\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\). Every adjacency and unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, is preserved, and for every \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
 \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\]
Consequently, if \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\ne\varnothing\), then a fully specified faithful replacement witness with all these properties exists. No equality between \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(\kappa(\eta)\) is asserted.
proposed.justification: The lemma now states exactly what graph preservation proves for fully specified members, with existence explicitly conditional on realization-fiber nonemptiness.
proposed.gap: It does not prove that an arbitrary admissible replacement fiber is nonempty.
proposed.consumer: It is the promotion step used whenever the separate faithful-realization premise supplies a member.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the unsupported nonemptiness dependency and retain the complete conditional characterization of every realization-fiber member.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\), where \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) is present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Let \(e\) be the endpoint at \(u\) on \(uv\). Then
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq \mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\]
Thus, if \(u\notin Z_k\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}\); if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\). If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the empty graph \(B_0\) on \(A(\eta)\) and the directed-edge graph \(B_P\) of any simple \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) are admissible and give two common-basal graphical replacement specifications preserving \(A(\eta)\) and every regime skeleton and unshielded collider on the full domains \(U_j\). The former has an arrowhead and the latter a tail at \(e\). In this two-mark case,
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\]
Here \(u\in Z_k\) denotes direct targeting or indirect affectedness within \(A(\eta)\), not necessarily \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this intervention-created-edge bracket.
proposed.justification: The theorem gives an unconditional outer bracket for faithful marks, exact identification in both singleton cases, and two explicit graphical specifications in the two-mark case.
proposed.gap: Opposing fully specified witnesses in the two-mark case still require nonempty faithful realization fibers.
proposed.consumer: It distinguishes endpoint marks already identified at fixed selection ancestry from graphical ambiguity that still awaits faithful promotion.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace unconditional opposing faithful witnesses by the proved faithful-model outer bracket, exact singleton cases, and conditional two-mark equality.

proposed.statement:
Does there exist a single finite rule list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with schemata independent of \(D\) and \(K\), that uses only the observable premises permitted by \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), is sound over every compatibility fiber, and has the following unknown-\(A\) graphical extension property? For every residual reported circle endpoint and each requested mark \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), the extension supplies a compatible base model and an admissible replacement graph, without guessing \(A\) in a rule premise or invoking a global feasibility query, such that every fully specified member of the corresponding realization fiber has mark \(m\). The affirmative answer must preserve the complete observational and pooled-law signatures, including indicator-involving adjacencies and unshielded colliders, and must respect
\[
 Z_k=T_k\cup\bigl((F_k\setminus T_k)\cap A\bigr)
\]
without setting \(T_k=Z_k\). Together with an affirmative answer to the faithful-realization question, this observable graphical extension property implies the conditional completeness theorem; neither affirmative answer is established here.
proposed.justification: This is the genuine remaining observable graphical-extension problem after the fixed-A bracket and faithful-realization problem are separated.
proposed.gap: No finite rule list is given that synchronizes unknown selection membership, one exterior basal completion, and every regime without a global feasibility query.
proposed.consumer: An affirmative answer, together with faithful realization, activates the conditional completeness theorem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Retain the unknown-selection common-exterior lift as a future problem and state exactly how it combines with faithful realization.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) be a candidate finite rule list whose schemata are independent of \(D\) and \(K\). Fix a compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\). Assume the following two conditions.

First, faithful realization holds: for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and every graph \(B\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma, \(\operatorname{Real}(\xi,B)\ne\varnothing\).

Second, the observable unknown-\(A\) extension property holds: the closure is sound, meaning that a definite mark \(m\) at \(e\) in \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) satisfies \(\mu_\xi(e)=m\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\); and, for every endpoint \(e\) left circular and every \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), there are \(\xi_{e,m}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and a graph \(B_{e,m}\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma such that every \(\widetilde\xi\in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m})\) has \(\mu_{\widetilde\xi}(e)=m\). The rule premises themselves use no latent \(A(\xi)\), compatible-model query, or global enumerator.

Then
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)
\]
on all reported observed endpoints. If, in addition, every rule premise and path predicate is uniformly decidable in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), then saturation is polynomial and makes at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. This is a conditional implication; it does not assert that either open condition or such a rule list exists.
proposed.justification: The theorem proves the endpointwise reduction from faithful realization and observable unknown-A graphical extension to canonical equality.
proposed.gap: It is conditional and proves neither the faithful-realization premise nor existence of a finite observable extension calculus.
proposed.consumer: It records exactly what the two open problems would certify and retains the conditional polynomial computation guarantee.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the unproved existence headline by the proved implication from the two explicitly stated future premises.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For every admissible replacement twin family and every query that is m-connected in its replacement MAG, exhibit an admissible equality-constrained shared-response-function parameter at which at least one conditional-independence determinant is nonzero.
open_obligations.obstruction: Unrestricted multinomial-DAG generic faithfulness does not imply nontriviality after the shared-response-function equalities, basal-event conditioning, and fixed pooled weight are imposed; the core does not specify a cross-world coupling that supplies the needed atomic witness.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced all simultaneous unfaithfulness events to finitely many determinant polynomials, proved the finite-union product argument on a nonempty open parameter set, and verified that positive local tables satisfy factorization, stability, and selection positivity. The reduction stops exactly at atomic determinant nontriviality.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any supplied nonempty open rational parameterization of the equality-constrained shared-response-function family, conditional independence is equivalent to finitely many cleared determinant-polynomial equations. If every \(m\)-connected query has one determinant polynomial that is not identically zero, the product of one such polynomial per query is nonzero and therefore is nonzero at some common parameter point; all pooled selected laws are then faithful simultaneously. Conversely, any simultaneously faithful point certifies nontriviality for every \(m\)-connected query. Positive local tables already satisfy factorization, non-target stability, and positive selection. Only the atomic nontriviality certificates on the constrained twin space remain unproved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a fixed finite observable rule list and prove the unknown-selection common-exterior graphical extension property for both marks at every residual circle, without latent-A rule premises or a global realizability query.
open_obligations.obstruction: Observable selectedness certificates provide only a sound subset of every feasible ancestral selected set. They do not locally choose the remaining selection membership and one exterior basal completion while preserving all regime fill edges and indicator collider signatures.
open_obligations.attempted: Combined the selectedness closure with the exact singleton fixed-A cases and the empty-graph/simple-path graphical specifications. These ingredients do not synchronize varying compatible ancestral selected sets or the shared exterior completion.
open_obligations.partial_result: Observable selectedness closure is sound, and the fixed-\(A\) theorem gives the nonempty bracket \(\mathcal M_A\subseteq\mathcal G_A\), exact singleton identification, and two signature-preserving graphical specifications in the two-mark case. If faithful realization is affirmative and a fixed observable rule list supplies the stated unknown-\(A\) graphical extension for both marks at every residual circle, then the conditional completeness theorem proves equality with the canonical SI-PAG and the existing saturation proposition gives polynomially many updates. No such finite unknown-\(A\) extension theorem is established.

prose_updates.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples all regime MAGs through one basal selected DAG. This round proves a graphical replacement theorem, a nonempty fixed-\(A(\eta)\) faithful-model mark bracket with exact singleton cases, and two signature-preserving graphical specifications for the two-mark case. It also proves that simultaneous faithfulness reduces to atomic determinant nontriviality and that faithful realization plus a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension theorem would imply equality of rule closure with the canonical SI-PAG and polynomial saturation. Faithful promotion and the finite extension calculus remain open, so no complete SI-PAG algorithm or opposing faithful-witness theorem is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain; their fixed-model endpoint semantics do not supply opposing common-basal faithful representatives. Zhang proves completeness for one observational PAG, not synchronized intervention regimes. Known-target enumeration results do not provide the required unknown-target, pre-treatment-selection local extension. The remaining gaps here are now isolated as atomic faithful realization and finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension.
project_justification.niche: The achieved contribution is a technical partial characterization for Dai et al.'s class: an observable selectedness certificate, a fixed-selection-ancestry graphical endpoint bracket, signature-preserving replacement specifications, and a conditional reduction to canonical completeness. This is not positioned as a field-level completeness result.
project_justification.fill: The note separates three layers. It proves graphical preservation and the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) mark-set inclusion, including exact singleton identifications; it proves the polynomial exceptional-set reduction for joint faithfulness; and it proves the endpointwise conditional implication from faithful realization and an observable unknown-\(A\) extension property to the canonical SI-PAG, with conditional polynomial saturation. It leaves both antecedents explicit and does not use global basal-DAG enumeration as a substitute.

sampling_model.design: Oracle graphical analysis from the observational MAG signature and \(K\) pooled intervention-regime MAG signatures generated by one common basal selected DAG. The canonical SI-PAG is the structural target; the established result is a partial fixed-\(A\) bracket and a conditional completeness reduction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable to the proved oracle results. The core supplies no finite-sample conditional-independence or invariance tests, separation margin, or simultaneous confidence theorem.

prose_updates.related_work: Dai et al.'s Lemmas 4--6 characterize intervention-created adjacencies, indicator neighborhoods, and endpoint semantics in the pre-treatment-selection twin class; their Theorem 3 establishes CDIS soundness, and their discussion leaves completeness uncertain. Zhang's Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for a single observational PAG, but do not synchronize several pooled intervention projections through one basal selected DAG. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes supply single-MAG equivalence invariants that motivate signature preservation, not common-basal realizability. The public Zhou--Kocaoglu abstract describes known-target completion by compatible-MAG enumeration and additional local tightening rules; this note neither imports a formula-level theorem from that inaccessible source nor claims a complete local replacement. Wang, Du, and Zhou inform only the conditional computational accounting. Jaber et al. address unknown-target interventions without selection, while Luo et al. address a distinct post-treatment-selection setting. Relative to all of these comparators, the present achievement is a fixed-\(A\) graphical bracket and conditional reduction, not completeness.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The replacement construction names a graphical specification, not a probability model. Signature preservation does not prove that its equality-constrained shared-response-function realization fiber contains a jointly faithful member. The exact residual statistical task is atomic determinant nontriviality for every m-connected query. Even if that task is solved, observable certificates identify only a subset of every compatible ancestral selected set; a finite local rule system must still synchronize unknown selectedness and one exterior basal completion across all regimes. The current results do not establish simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs, because no finite-sample testing assumptions, separation margin, or error-control theorem is present in the frozen core.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Proved content consists of the graphical replacement preservation lemma already in the core; the conditional characterization of every fully specified replacement-fiber member; the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) inclusion \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A\subseteq\mathcal G_A\), with exact tail-only and arrow-only cases; empty-graph and simple-path signature-preserving graphical specifications in the two-mark case; the finite algebraic exceptional-set reduction; and the conditional endpointwise completeness and polynomial-saturation implications. Nonemptiness of arbitrary replacement realization fibers, opposing faithful witnesses in the two-mark case, a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) rule list, unconditional equality with the canonical SI-PAG, and simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees remain open. The scope is finite-alphabet, causally sufficient, childless pre-treatment selection with pooled binary-indicator regime laws; latent common causes, post-treatment selection, regime-specific selection mechanisms, and a global basal-DAG enumerator as headline calculus are excluded. The achieved positioning is therefore a rigorous technical foundation and partial characterization, explicitly below a field-level completeness contribution.
